articles.title: Pickford or Trafford? Has the battle to be England's number one started?
articles.summary: Jordan Pickford has been England's number one for a long time. But does he now have a rival in James Trafford?
articles.body:
You have to go back 10 years to find a major tournament where Jordan Pickford was not starting in goal for England.

The Everton goalkeeper has pretty much been England's number one since making his debut in 2017 - until now.

Saturday's 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain saw Leeds' James Trafford make his competitive debut for the Three Lions as manager Thomas Tuchel signalled the battle to be number one is on.

Pickford became England's highest appearance maker at World Cups, overtaking Peter Shilton when he started in England's 2026 quarter-final win over Norway.

During Gareth Southgate's tenure there was not a natural goalkeeper to rival Pickford, and that looked to continue under Tuchel as Pickford started all but one of England's World Cup qualifiers and then every game in the summer.

But it looks as though Pickford has finally got a rival in Trafford, with Tuchel saying that the pair get "two consecutive matches each" during this international break.

Trafford has impressed since making his move to Leeds for a deal worth up to £45m.

Against Spain, the 23-year-old showed his quality with the ball at his feet and made an impressive save to deny Ferran Torres in the first half.

But he was beaten three times as England lost their Nations League opener to the world champions.

"I think he deserved to get the two matches, that's why we gave him two matches," Tuchel said.

"He started the Premier League season well and gets minutes as number one at Leeds.

"Jordan [Pickford] did absolutely nothing wrong but we wanted to use this competition to see how far actually James is."

Trafford's journey to possible England number one

Trafford's form this season has helped Leeds to fifth in the Premier League table.

He has kept two clean sheets and now has his chance to stake his claim as England's future number one over two matches.

Trafford had only played 32 top-flight games before moving to Leeds following time at Burnley and Manchester City.

He came through City's academy and joined Burnley for an initial fee of £15m in the summer of 2023.

However, he conceded 67 goals in only 28 matches before losing his place towards the end of the 2023-24 season.

But after starring in Burnley's successful promotion in 2024-25 and the Clarets conceding just 16 goals, Trafford returned to City for £27m last summer with the hope of being Pep Guardiola's number one.

City brought in one of the best goalkeepers in the world in Gianluigi Donnarumma, just four weeks after Trafford's arrival and he became second choice.

Despite it being a frustrating campaign, Trafford did get vital experience and started both the FA Cup final and Carabao Cup final for City before his move to Leeds.

He has been part of England success too, winning the U21 European Championship in 2023 and saving a stoppage-time penalty as Lee Carsley's side beat Spain in the final.

Pickford has been England's reliable keeper

Pickford has kept 46 clean sheets in his 91 appearances for England and has been a huge part of the Three Lions' recent success at major tournaments.

"I think Jordan Pickford will be very disappointed," former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Putting myself in that place, he will be questioning why he is not in that place. If he is number one, then why is he not playing against the world champions?

"You wonder whether this is the next generation coming through for Thomas Tuchel."

Pickford put in an excellent performance as England beat Mexico in the World Cup to progress to the quarter-finals, but it was not the goalkeeper's best tournament.

"Jordan Pickford has never let England down," Ian Dennis said.

"You have opposition against the Czech Republic and Croatia where you could give James Trafford an opportunity then. I do find the decision quite strange.

"Pickford against the world champions - you would back him to play in this game."

Pickford is in current possession of the number one shirt and played every minute of the World Cup until he was rested for England's third-place play-off win over France, with Dean Henderson starting.

The 32-year-old, who will be 34 at Euro 2028, has 91 England caps and has saved four of the 14 penalties he has faced in major tournament shootouts.

In the Premier League Pickford's overall numbers dwarf Trafford's. Since the start of the 2024-25 season no-one has prevented more expected goals than the Everton stopper.

But there is very little between the two this campaign with Pickford preventing more goals but Trafford having a higher save percentage and better passing accuracy.

Pickford has been fantastic for England but he didn't have the best World Cup, with a couple conceded that arguably he should've saved and a few nervy moments playing out from the back. Now seems as good a time as any to try James Trafford.

James Trafford deserves to start, he's going to be England's next number one and why not start him against Spain or would you rather he only played against third-rate nations?

James Trafford deserves his shot! Jordan Pickford has been quality for 10 years! Time feels right to test who could be next. Finding the next Harry Kane is going to be the problem!

Jordan Pickford is paying the price for those mistakes creeping in during the World Cup. Could he have stopped the goals v Croatia, DR Congo and Fernandez v Argentina? Prime Pickford does. Thomas Tuchel showing his ruthless side again.

articles.title: El Sant Andreu aprovechó la osadía del Nàstic
articles.standfirst: Una acción en el 96’, cuando los locales estaban completamente volcados al ataque, supuso el 1-2 que dejaba en nada un golazo de Carlos Segura
articles.summary: Una acción en el 96’, cuando los locales estaban completamente volcados al ataque, supuso el 1-2 que dejaba en nada un golazo de Carlos Segura
articles.body: Hay derrotas que duelen por lo que se escapa en el último suspiro, y el Gimnàstic de Tarragona probó ese sabor amargo en la quinta jornada de Primera Federación. Cuando el partido parecía encaminado al reparto de puntos, apareció Alexis García en el minuto 90 para firmar el 1-2 definitivo y darle a la UE Sant Andreu un triunfo tan trabajado como valioso lejos de casa. El delantero, que había entrado en el campo apenas diecinueve minutos antes, decidió un choque que el Nàstic había reconducido con carácter tras verse por detrás. FICHA TÉCNICA Nàstic. Ayesa; Oriol (Eugeni, 84’), Joseda, Athuman, Royo, Almansa; Montalvo, Meshak (Shin, 90’), Borja (Segura, 69’); Prohens (Pere Marco, 84’) y Bakis (Diego Gómez, 69’). Sant Andreu. Iñaki; Méndez, Montoro, Andreu, Carrasco (Menéndez, 99¡), Viña; Torices, Delgado; Serrano (Albertito, 84’), Armero (Tovar, 70’) y Bermejo (Alexis, 70’). Goles. 0-1, Bermejo de penalti (56’); 1-1, Segura (71’). 1-2, Alexis (96’). Árbitro. Sergio Escriche. Amarillas a los locales Joseda, Royo, Segura y Montalvo; y a los visitantes Serrano, Torices y Viña. Un penalti abrió el camino visitante El primer tiempo se cerró sin goles (0-0 al descanso), con dos conjuntos igualados que se estudiaron sin concesiones. Todo cambió en la segunda mitad. En el minuto 56, casi en la misma acción en la que José Menargues vio la tarjeta amarilla por el lado local, el Sant Andreu golpeó desde los once metros: Álex Bermejo Escribano transformó el penalti para poner el 0-1 y silenciar a la grada tarraconense. El gol obligó al Nàstic a moverse, y su técnico no tardó en agitar el banquillo. En el minuto 69 entraron Diego Gómez y Carlos Segura por Sinan Bakış y Borja Sánchez, y la apuesta ofensiva dio réditos casi de inmediato. En el 71, Carlos Segura firmó el empate a uno, premio a la reacción de un equipo que se lanzó a por el partido y que durante un buen tramo pareció el más cercano a la remontada. Golpe final en el 90 La igualada, sin embargo, no calmó las aguas. El partido se volvió intenso y bronco —el árbitro repartió amonestaciones a ambos lados, con Sergi Serrano, Daniel Torices, Manel Royo, el propio Carlos Segura, Marc Montalvo y Emilio Lucas entre los señalados— y el Nàstic buscó incluso completar el vuelco, dando entrada a Pere Marco, Eugeni Valderrama y Shinnosuke Katsushima en el tramo final. Pero fue el Sant Andreu el que encontró el premio. En el minuto 90, Alexis García aprovechó su frescura para batir a Gaizka Ayesa y establecer el 1-2 definitivo. El curioso detalle es que Alexis había sustituido precisamente a Bermejo, el autor del primer tanto visitante: los dos goles del conjunto de Sant Andreu llevaron la firma del once y del recambio que lo relevó, un cambio que salió redondo. Contexto de clasificación: un duelo de vecinos en la tabla El resultado tiene lecturas directas en la zona media del Grupo 2. La UE Sant Andreu, que llegaba empatada con el Nàstic, se coloca ahora con 2 victorias, 1 empate y 2 derrotas para un balance de 7 puntos en el séptimo puesto, con cinco goles a favor y cinco en contra. El triunfo le permite respirar y mantenerse enganchada a la parte noble de una tabla comprimida. El Gimnàstic, por su parte, se queda igualmente con 7 puntos (2 victorias, 1 empate y 2 derrotas) y siete goles a favor por siete en contra, ocupando la octava posición justo por detrás de su verdugo. Es un arranque de curso irregular para los tarraconenses, que suman ya dos derrotas en cinco jornadas y ven cómo la cabeza del grupo, con el Villarreal B U23 líder con 13 puntos y el Real Zaragoza segundo con 12, empieza a marcar distancias. La imagen de la tabla en la zona alta refleja lo apretado del pelotón perseguidor: Real Jaén (10 puntos), Real Murcia (9) y Hércules CF (9) presionan por arriba, mientras que un puñado de equipos se agolpa entre los 5 y los 8 puntos. En ese contexto, cada punto pesa, y el que el Sant Andreu arrebató en Tarragona puede valer doble cuando el campeonato madure. Jugadores a seguir El nombre del día es Alexis García. Su irrupción desde el banquillo cambió el guion y su gol en el 90 fue el de un futbolista que sabe leer los minutos finales. En una liga tan igualada, tener recursos así en la recámara marca diferencias. Junto a él, Álex Bermejo Escribano confirmó por qué es una de las referencias ofensivas del Sant Andreu: sangre fría desde el punto de penalti para abrir el marcador y poner a su equipo por delante en el momento clave del choque. En el bando local, Carlos Segura salió del banquillo para empatar y mantener vivo al Nàstic. Su gol demostró que el conjunto tarraconense tiene revulsivos, aunque esta vez no bastara para sumar. Es un futbolista a vigilar si el Gimnàstic quiere reengancharse a la pelea por los puestos de privilegio. Conclusión Fue un partido de pulso, tarjetas y decisiones de banquillo, resuelto por el detalle más caro del fútbol: un gol en el descuento. El Sant Andreu se marcha de Tarragona con tres puntos que lo sitúan por delante de su rival directo, mientras el Gimnàstic lamenta un empate que se le convirtió en derrota en el último minuto. Con la clasificación tan estrecha en el Grupo 2, ambos saben que el margen de error es mínimo. Para el Nàstic toca reaccionar; para el Sant Andreu, confirmar que este triunfo no es un espejismo.

articles.title: Iowa Stuns Bryce Underwood, Michigan as Time Expires, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Reaction
articles.summary: No. 17 Iowa defeated Bryce Underwood and No. 18 Michigan as time ran out on Saturday, winning by the final score of 20-19 in Ann Arbor.
articles.body:
No. 17 Iowa defeated Bryce Underwood and No. 18 Michigan as time ran out on Saturday, winning by the final score of 20-19 in Ann Arbor.

As the Hawkeyes faced a five-point deficit with two seconds left in the fourth quarter and the ball at the Wolverines' 16-yard line, Iowa quarterback Hank Brown found Reece Vander Zee for the game-winning score.

It marked the first loss of the 2026 season for Underwood and Michigan.

Fans and pundits were shocked by Iowa's win, referencing Michigan's controversial season-opening victory over Western Michigan.

Both offenses started off slow on Saturday, trading punts before Michigan finally began to move the ball down the field.

The Wolverines drove to Iowa's 18-yard line before Underwood connected with JJ Buchanan for a touchdown on third down.

Michigan wasn't able to consistently move the chains for the remainder of the first half, although head coach Kyle Whittingham's squad still held a 10-7 lead at halftime.

The Wolverines entered Iowa's red zone once again near the start of the third quarter, but Underwood was picked off to end the possession.

Michigan's defense still held firm, as Iowa couldn't get on the board before the third quarter came to a close.

The Wolverines held a 13-7 advantage heading into the fourth, although the Hawkeyes took their first lead of the game with a 16-yard touchdown pass from Brown to Vander Zee.

Michigan didn't take long to respond, however.

On the Wolverines' next drive, Underwood danced in the pocket before launching a deep pass to Buchanan for a 49-yard score.

Iowa's hopes took another hit after a missed a field goal on its next drive, but the Hawkeyes' defense was able to force a Michigan punt and give the team one final shot.

With only one minute and 37 seconds left in the fourth, the Hawkeyes pieced together a 91-yard drive that was capped off by Brown's touchdown pass.

Vander Zee finished with 66 yards and two scores on five catches for Iowa, while Tony Diaz also hauled in three receptions for 46 yards.

The Wolverines fell to 3-1 with the defeat, while the Hawkeyes stayed undefeated and improved to 4-0.

articles.title: CFB Playoff Picture, Standings and Bracket Predictions After Week 4 of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The SEC is such a beast of a conference that the Ole Miss Rebels can be the kings of the sport one week and the victim of an upset one week later.
articles.body:
The SEC is such a beast of a conference that the Ole Miss Rebels can be the kings of the sport one week and the victim of an upset one week later.

Trinidad Chambliss and Co. fell on the road to the Florida Gators, one week after they knocked off Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers at home.

In the 12-team College Football Playoff era, one loss won't derail a program's playoff prospects, but the defeat does cool some of the heat that was behind Ole Miss after last week.

While Ole Miss will drop a bit in the Week 5 rankings, the same team will reside at the top.

The Texas Longhorns moved to 4-0 with a defensive-dominated road win over the Tennessee Volunteers.

The CFB Playoff projections are based on results through Saturday afternoon's games.

The Florida Gators entered their name into the CFB Playoff conversation with their 52-28 thumping of Ole Miss in Gainesville.

Jon Sumrall's team moved to 4-0 with the victory over the fourth-ranked team in the country.

The win was a statement of intent in Sumrall's first season in charge.

The Gators will likely jump from No. 21 further up the AP Top 25 on Sunday, but they might not reach the top 12 just yet.

There are opportunities, though, for the Gators to climb since they still have to play No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia.

However, the big game in Florida's playoff case could be next week at Missouri. If the Gators win in Missouri and only lose to Texas and Georgia, they have a compelling case as 10-2 at-large team.

As for Ole Miss, it will drop a bit in the standings, but its resume still has two ranked wins over LSU and Louisville.

Ole Miss also has Texas and UGA on its remaining schedule, as well as Missouri and Mississippi State among the top 25 teams in the SEC.

The Rebels will be competitive in most games because of Trinidad Chambliss, but they need to figure out the defense that has now allowed 38 and 52 points in two of four games this season.

Texas Keeps Rolling With Win Over Tennessee

Texas left Knoxville with a 4-0 record because of its defense.

The Longhorns recorded 10 sacks, five of which came from star pass-rusher Colin Simmons, in the 20-17 victory.

Arch Manning didn't have the best game, but he did push the Texas offense down the field in the fourth quarter to produce an important touchdown.

Texas is now 4-0 with a road Top 25 win in the SEC and a home victory over the Ohio State Buckeyes.

Texas still has six ranked opponents on its SEC schedule, but at least for now, it rest for a week with an undefeated record.

The Longhorns are next in action on October 10 in their annual rivalry clash with the Oklahoma Sooners. After that, five consecutive ranked foes face Texas. We'll find out more about the Longhorns during that stretch.

articles.title: Ole Miss Loses to Florida After Kiffin Win, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Chambliss, Top Players
articles.summary: Ole Miss was unable to carry the momentum of last weekend's revenge victory over Lane Kiffin and LSU into Saturday's showdown with Florida.
articles.body:
Ole Miss was unable to carry the momentum of last weekend's revenge victory over Lane Kiffin and LSU into Saturday's showdown with Florida.

Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss turned the ball over twice, while Gators running back Jadan Baugh scored three touchdowns as No. 21 Florida secured a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss.

Here's a look at the top offensive performers from Florida's upset win.

Baugh helped the Gators grab an early lead with a touchdown run on the game's opening drive.

The Gators' defense followed up that effort by ending Ole Miss' first offensive possession with a lost fumble on fourth-and-1.

Ole Miss made the matchup a one-score game by recording a 35-yard field goal in the second quarter.

Baugh helped the Gators extend their lead by running in his second touchdown of the game in the second quarter.

The star running back has now scored multiple touchdowns in all four of Florida's games so far this season.

Ole Miss ended the first half with a field goal before forcing a three-and-out. Chambliss then opened the third quarter by running in a touchdown to get his team within three points of tying the game.

That started out a high-scoring stretch during which both teams completed back-to-back touchdown drives.

Ole Miss still trailed at the end of that stretch, which ended when Chambliss lost a fumble. Florida capitalized with a touchdown to extend their lead.

Baugh ran in his third score of the day late in the fourth quarter before DJ Coleman picked off Chambliss to close out the win.

Ole Miss finished out the loss having allowed 498 total yards against (302 on the ground), while Florida allowed 426 yards against (298 passing).

The Gators are now off to their first 4-0 start since 2019 . Florida should see a nice bump in its ranking before taking on another ranked opponent in No. 19 Missouri.

Ole Miss, which is primed to take a hit in next week's rankings, will look to bounce back Saturday at Vanderbilt.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 4
articles.summary: Florida is surging, Oklahoma is falling, there was another last-second finish at Michigan and plenty more happened in a hectic Saturday of college football.
articles.body:
Florida is surging, Oklahoma is falling, there was another last-second finish at Michigan and plenty more happened in a hectic Saturday of college football.

Oh, and Jeremiah Smith is still ridiculous.

As conference play ratcheted up across the country, Week 4 brought a flood of fantastic matchups. Six games featured a pair of Top 25 teams, and three of those showdowns are under the prime-time lights.

Beyond those marquee results, Wake Forest also provided a significant upset with a victory at No. 16 Louisville.

We're closely following the busy day and sharing key takeaways from the action.

Following a record-breaking performance last weekend, Jeremiah Smith straight-up destroyed the Illinois secondary on Saturday.

Ohio State rolled to a 42-19 win behind 12 catches for 217 yards and four touchdowns from its superstar wideout.

Each one of those numbers set a career high for Smith, who is surging toward a third straight All-American honor. Plus, with 617 yards and seven scores in September, he's becoming a strong contender for the Heisman Trophy.

Iowa, which has been among the nation's top pass defenses early on, awaits Smith and the Buckeyes in Week 5.

Well that wasn't the encore Louisville wanted.

After taking down SMU in a key Top 25 matchup last weekend, the Cardinals turned around and lost 30-27 at home to Wake Forest.

The worst part is how many chances Louisville had to survive. The offense's three drives in the fourth quarter ended with a turnover on downs at the Wake 38, a missed 42-yard field goal and a blocked 57-yarder.

So much for being the ACC's main threat to Miami, huh?

Louisville still has a very favorable slate remaining and shouldn't disappear from the conference race, but its margin for error has vanished.

I often think of a mic'd up moment from San Francisco 49ers edge-rusher Nick Bosa. He turned to a teammate on the sideline and said : "I just want to sack the quarterback, dude. It's not as easy as it looks."

Colin Simmons certainly made it look simple on Saturday.

While helping Texas pull out a 20-17 road victory, the junior tore apart Tennessee's offensive line with five sacks. Simmons even had a half-sack negated due to a penalty, so he settled for tying a program record and instead of breaking it.

"I've never seen anything like that," Texas linebacker Justin Cryer told reporters . "He's the best defensive player in the country."

Simmons already had a very positive reputation, and a signature performance in a spotlight game only bolsters his prestige.

There's no sense in sugarcoating the situation at Oklahoma, which has a giant, stinky mess on its hands offensively.

Mustering 289 yards in a 17-10 loss to Michigan threw up red flags, and only putting up 299 yards in a 14-6 win over New Mexico sounded some alarms. Saturday's meltdown at Georgia has sent OU into panic mode.

John Mateer's bizarre red-zone fumble—which UGA's Chris Cole returned for a touchdown—kickstarted the wreck. Mateer threw an interception of the next possession, then lost a fumble.

Throw in a fourth fumble and a missed field goal, and Oklahoma hardly could have endured a worse afternoon in a 41-13 loss.

Especially since OU has an open weekend ahead, expect some personnel changes. Given that six ranked teams are left on the Sooners' schedule, however, the odds of a turnaround aren't exactly high.

Earlier in the week, UF coach Jon Sumrall gave a humorous response when a reporter said the Gators were favored over No. 4 Ole Miss.

Florida, uh—Florida covered that three-point spread.

Ole Miss failed to find a single solution to contain the Gators, who racked up 498 yards in a 52-28 rout of the Rebels.

Star running back Jadan Baugh scampered for 142 yards with three trips to the end zone, while Duke Clark chipped in 126 yards and a score. Aaron Philo passed for a modest 196 yards but spread the ball around efficiently, accounted for two touchdowns and didn't have any turnovers.

Most impressively, the Gators went 5-for-5 on touchdown drives in the second half before draining the clock on their last possession.

Florida has a tough October ahead with Missouri, Texas and rival Georgia on the docket. But so far, this offense is one of the country's most dangerous units.

Back in Week 1, Michigan seemed to have fallen to Western Michigan. One controversial replay decision and an incredible Hail Mary later, the Wolverines escaped with a contentious 13-12 victory.

Call it fitting, karma, whatever you want—Michigan found itself on the other side of the last-second drama in Week 4.

Trailing 19-14 in the final minute, Iowa tight end Addison Ostrenga pulled down a tipped ball for a wild 29-yard catch. The clock stopped with two seconds left, giving the Hawkeyes one snap from the 16-yard line. Hank Brown zipped a perfect back-shoulder ball to Reece Vander Dee for a touchdown as time expired.

Michigan was fortunate to beat WMU. This was an unlucky loss.

And, man, if that's not college football in a nutshell.

One victory does not undo the recent struggles of Wisconsin under Luke Fickell. During his three seasons, the Badgers have dipped from 7-6 to 5-7 to 4-8 with their Big Ten record worsening each year, too.

Fickell entered the campaign knowing the team needed to improve—not just on paper, in the win column specifically.

Saturday's upset of 13th-ranked Penn State was a massive result for Fickell.

Wisconsin trailed 17-0 but stormed back to win 24-20, riding a dominant defense in the second half and finding a late, remarkable 72-yard touchdown from tight end Jacob Harris. It wasn't the fastest sprint , but it was effective!

The tone of this conversation is liable to change in a hurry. Falling to Michigan State next week, for example, would negate the happiness of this win.

Fickell, nevertheless, just landed a much-needed boost.

articles.title: Michigan football winners, losers as special teams flub too costly
articles.summary: Free Press sports writer Rainer Sabin highlights the best and worst performances from No. 18 Michigan football's 20-19 loss to No. 17 Iowa.
articles.body:
Free Press sports writer Rainer Sabin highlights the best and worst performances from No. 18 Michigan football 's 20-19 loss to No. 17 Iowa on Saturday, Sept. 26, at Michigan Stadium.

Ever since his rough 2026 debut against Western Michigan, Underwood has looked more competent and poised while operating the Wolverines ' offense. On Saturday, he jumped out to a fast start, connecting on eight of his first 10 throws for 118 yards and a touchdown. If not for a Salesi Moa drop on Underwood's second pass attempt, Underwood's completion percentage would have even been higher. Coordinator Jason Beck put Underwood in position to succeed by utilizing his athleticism. On several occasions, he called plays with designed rollouts that gave Underwood clear throwing lanes downfield. Beck also creatively deployed Underwood in a Wildcat package, lining him up out wide and having him flash across the formation in a jet motion. In one instance, Underwood took a handoff from running back Jordan Marshall and then completed an 11-yard pass to Andrew Marsh . Later in the half, Beck dipped again into his bag of tricks, dialing up a flea-flicker. Underwood executed it to perfection, feathering a layered pass to JJ Buchanan for a 32-yard gain.

In the fourth quarter, after Iowa took the one-point lead, Underwood maneuvered in the pocket, evaded a few oncoming rushers and delivered a 49-yard strike to Buchanan to put the Wolverines ahead, 19-14.

It seemed at that point his touchdown pass would carry Michigan to its fourth win. Alas, it was not meant to be . Still, Underwood could walk away knowing he authored one of the best performances of his career. He finished the game with 17 completions on 28 attempts, 276 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception.

See Michigan football vs Iowa at Big House in ranked Big Ten opener

While no one would claim Michigan has an elite passing offense, the Wolverines do have a pair of talented wideouts who possess dynamic playmaking ability.

That was evident Saturday, as Marsh and Buchanan took turns singing Iowa 's defense.

On Michigan's second possession, Marsh helped carry Michigan into Hawkeyes territory with two catches that totaled 47 yards. The second one was a remarkable feat of athleticism, as Marsh leapt to snag a pass from Underwood along the sideline while managing to keep one of his feet inbounds. Six plays later, Underwood connected with Buchanan for an 18-yard touchdown, as the Utah transfer outmaneuvered Iowa defensive back Ty Brown to snatch the ball in the end zone.

By the end of the game, Buchanan had contributed five catches for 130 yards and two touchdowns. Marsh, meanwhile, produced seven receptions for 106 yards.

In a game like this one, where the margin for error was expected to be thin, Michigan couldn't afford many mistakes.

But the Wolverines had a major breakdown a few seconds after they took a 7-0 lead in the first quarter. On the kickoff that followed Buchanan's 18-yard touchdown catch, Iowa returner Braeden Jackson fielded the ball at the 1, veered right and found an alley. By the time he reached the 30, he was in the clear. Jackson zipped all the way to the end zone. The 99-yard return tied the score and stunned the home crowd.

It also reverberated for the rest of the game, keeping Iowa within striking distance of the Wolverines and boosting a team that managed to produce just 129 yards through the first three quarters.

Throughout its history, Michigan has extracted a lot of production out of its tight ends. Two years ago, Colston Loveland led the Wolverines in receiving en route to an NFL draft first-round selection.

But through the first three games, U-M's passing game was powered almost entirely by U-M's wide receivers and running backs.

Jalen Hoffman was the lone tight end to catch a pass and he accounted for just two receptions for 22 yards. On Tuesday, when asked what needed to change for his position group to become more involved, sophomore Eli Owens said, "Obviously, what jumps off the page is we need to get open. I mean, that's everybody in the room. We need to get open. That's simply what it is."

Michigan tight ends again weren't much of a factor Saturday against Iowa.

Collectively, they contributed just four catches for 21 yards.

For much of the game, the Wolverines' fifth-year player was one of Michigan's top performers.

Targeted seven times, he allowed just three catches for 15 yards. He also produced two pass breakups, according to Pro Football Focus.

But none of that mattered when he committed an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty during Iowa's final drive, shoving receiver Tony Diaz after a pass toward the sideline fell incomplete. If the foul had not been committed, Iowa would have faced fourth-and-12 at its own 40. Instead the Hawkeyes began a new set of downs at Michigan's 45. Four snaps after that pivotal moment, Iowa quarterback Hank Brown connected with Reece Vander Zee for on a 16-yard touchdown pass as time expired, lifting the Hawkeyes to an improbable one-point victory.

Certainly, Berry was not the sole reason why the Wolverines lost. But his penalty helped position the Hawkeyes to steal the win.

articles.title: How long had it been since Auburn football won an SEC home game?
articles.summary: When was Auburn football's last SEC home win before beating Vanderbilt Saturday? It had been quite a while.
articles.body:
AUBURN — It definitely felt like it'd been a long while, but with Auburn football beating Vanderbilt , the program saw one of its ugliest losing streaks come to an end.

The result marked head coach Alex Golesh 's first SEC victory, yes, but the last time the Tigers had beaten a league opponent at home?

It'd been nearly two years. One year, 10 months and three days, to be exact. Before taking care of the Commodores in a 21-15 result Saturday, Sept. 26, Auburn 's last SEC win at Jordan-Hare Stadium came Nov. 23, 2024, when it beat a ranked Texas A&M team in a four-overtime thriller.

"I don't know if I look at it quite big picture like that," Golesh said postgame in reference to the topic. "It was really, really good to beat a good football team. It was good to win in the SEC, it was good to win at home. ... I can't control what happened before I got here. I can only control what we do now; right here, right now."

That losing streak was seemingly a credit, rather a discredit, to Golesh's predecessor, Hugh Freeze. In all, Auburn went 3-11 in SEC home games with Freeze at the helm; one of many garishly disappointing feathers in Freeze's cap.

Auburn went 6-16 against the league and 9-11 at home under Freeze, but with Saturday's victory, Golesh finds himself separated from Freeze in one standpoint.

Of Auburn's last 10 head coaches, seven won their first SEC game. Two others got their first league victory on the second try, but Freeze was the only exception of that stretch, needing five league games to find a win.

The two Auburn coaches who didn't get an league victory until their second try? Golesh and Pat Dye.

articles.summary: Texas A&M football plays LSU on Sept. 26, 2026 in Baton Rouge. Here are live updates from the game and how to watch Saturday night.
articles.body:
Texas A&M football might already be in must-win mode.

Two losses doesn't eliminate a team from College Football Playoff contention, but with two months of the regular season left, it eliminates much of a program's margin for error. LSU suffered its first loss last week to Ole Miss while Texas A&M fell to Kentucky . That means two teams ranked in the top-10 at one point this season have precarious footing as September ends.

The good news for the Aggies is they have handled LSU well in the recent past. Mike Elko is 2-0 against the Bayou Bengals and A&M has won three of the last four matchups. The bad news is Lane Kiffin wasn't the Tigers' head coach for any of those games, and he's leading LSU now.

Last week, quarterback Marcel Reed was 26 of 49 for 236 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, adding a rushing score. Rueben Owens II rushed for 74 yards on 18 carries and Reed, with 80 yards, was A&M's top rusher. Mario Craver had 11 catches for 119 yards; Reed targeted him 19 times.

The bigger issue last week was that Kentucky quarterback Kenny Minchey was 14 of 18 for 252 yards and two touchdowns against the Aggies at Kyle Field. Former Longhorns CJ Baxter rushed for 87 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt has the mobility to give A&M fits and LSU averages more than 200 rush yards per game.

articles.title: Iowa Trolls Michigan's Controversial Hail Mary Win vs. WMU After Walk-Off TD
articles.summary: Iowa joked about Michigan's controversial season-opening win over Western Michigan after the Hawkeyes secured a 20-19 victory against the Wolverines on Saturday.
articles.body:
Iowa joked about Michigan's controversial season-opening win over Western Michigan after the Hawkeyes secured a 20-19 victory against the Wolverines on Saturday.

After Iowa scored a game-winning touchdown as the clock ran out, it wrote that there was "no extra time necessary" in a post on X.

The Wolverines previously took down Western Michigan by the final score of 13-12 with a Hail Mary to begin the year.

Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's initial Hail Mary attempt failed as time appeared to expire, although officials determined that one second remained on the game clock before the team's second try was successful.

Iowa made sure to remind fans that it didn't require any additional time for its walk-off win, improving to 4-0 on the season as a result.

articles.title: No. 13 Penn State Upset by Wisconsin After Blowing 17-Point Lead, Final Box Score Stats and Reaction
articles.summary: No. 13 Penn State blew a 17-point first-half lead en route to a 24-20 home loss to Wisconsin on Saturday.
articles.body:
No. 13 Penn State blew a 17-point first-half lead en route to a 24-20 home loss to Wisconsin on Saturday.

Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph fired touchdown passes to Eugene Hilton Jr. (11 yards, with 3:31 left) and Jacob Harris (72 yards, with 1:13 remaining) to turn a 20-10 fourth-quarter deficit into a 24-20 lead.

The Badgers were in serious trouble on the drive leading to the Harris score and faced a 2nd-and-19 on their own six-yard line. However, Joseph hit Darrion Dupree for 25 yards before connecting with Harris for the game-winning score.

Penn State had a minute-and-change to drive down the field and got as far as the Wisconsin 29-yard line but could not go any further after a sack and three incomplete passes led to time running out.

articles.title: Mistakes, injuries sink Michigan State in frustrating loss to Nebraska
articles.summary: Michigan State football made too many mistakes and suffered too many injuries in a Week 4 loss to Nebraska at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 26.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING – Michigan State football made too many mistakes and suffered too many injuries to have a chance in a 31-13 Week 4 loss to Nebraska at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 26.

The Spartans lost their best player on offense ( Cam Edwards , knee), their best player on defense ( Jordan Hall , leg) and were playing without the top-four cornerbacks in the frustrating game vs. the Cornhuskers . They also had two fumbles (one lost) and two interceptions, not to mention multiple costly penalties.

At times, the Spartans looked like they belonged, but there were some bad mistakes and some bad breaks that ultimately were too much to overcome in what ended up being an ugly game.

See Michigan State football open Big Ten play vs Nebraska at home

MSU's defense, which has been decimated by injuries at cornerback and already playing without starting linebacker Brady Pretzlaff before the injury to Hall, held in the fight, producing stops on the first three drives to start the second half.

After scoring a field goal on their first drive after the break, the Spartans fumbled on their second drive and then were driving down the field on their third drive when tight end Jayden Savoury made what looked like an incredible catch to get the Spartans into prime scoring position, but the catch was ultimately overturned by a tough review.

Quarterback Alessio Milivojevic , who was under pressure all day with six Nebraska sacks, fumbled again and though it was recovered by MSU this time, the Spartans missed their 52-yard field goal attempt to come out empty handed, and the Cornhuskers cruised to a victory from there.

The Spartans return to the road to face Wisconsin next Saturday, Oct. 3 in Madison, Wisconsin (12:30 p.m./BTN). This will be the first time MSU has faced a Luke Fickell coached team since he spurned the Spartans for a chance to replace Mark Dantonio after he retired in February 2020. Fickell instead remained at Cincinnati until he took over in Madison in 2023.

The Badgers (2-1, who lost their opener to Notre Dame), opened conference play at No. 14 Penn State on Saturday concurrent with the MSU-Nebraska game. Fickell, in his fourth season at Wisconsin, entered Saturday with a 19-22 overall record and a 10-17 Big Ten record. Dantonio and MSU beat Ohio State , 10-7, in 2011 when Fickell was interim head coach after Jim Tressel's firing.
